text:
anita: Hey team — trying to wire up cross-tenant access: central encryption service lives in the infra tenant (central-kv). We want resources in the PCI tenant to use a managed identity to call Key Vault data plane (wrap/unwrap). MSI fails with 403. Anyone hit this?

sam: Managed identities are tenant-scoped. You can't use a system-assigned MSI from tenant A to directly authenticate against a Key Vault in tenant B. The token audience and object id live in the originating tenant.

carlos: FWIW we tried Azure Lighthouse for cross-tenant ops but that is for ARM (management) plane only. Key Vault data plane still expects a principal from the key vault's tenant to be authorized.

liz: Short options: invite a service principal from the calling tenant as a guest in the KV tenant and grant Key Vault Data roles, or create an app registration/service principal in the KV tenant and hand out client creds. Another pragmatic option is a tiny per-tenant proxy (service in PCI tenant) that has a user-assigned identity and talks to central service over a controlled API.

mike: Prefer Azure RBAC (Key Vault Data roles) over legacy access policies where possible — role assignments are easier to manage for SPs/MSIs. Note: access policies are identity-object-id specific and can be a pain across tenants.

anita: Good to know. For the envelope encryption piece: does team prefer using KV to wrap DEKs (KEK) or using a local HSM to wrap? Also looking for rotation best-practices (we need frequent rotation for PCI).

sam: Best practice: use Key Vault (Managed HSM if you need FIPS/attestation) as the KEK. Pattern: generate DEK (AES-256) locally, wrap it with Key Vault key (RSA-OAEP or AES-KW), store wrapped DEK next to ciphertext. On decrypt, unwrap via KV. For rotation: either proactive rewrap all stored DEKs to new key version, or lazy rewrap (rewrap on first decrypt). Always record the key_id and key_version used to wrap each DEK.

Example CLI for wrap/unwrap:
```bash
# wrap DEK (base64 DEK -> wrapped blob base64)
az keyvault key wrap --vault-name prod-kv --name kek-key --algorithm RSA-OAEP --value "$(echo -n $DEK | base64)"

# unwrap
az keyvault key unwrap --vault-name prod-kv --name kek-key --algorithm RSA-OAEP --value <wrapped-base64>
```

carlos: Also: enable soft-delete + purge-protection on KV (set purge protection to prevent accidental destruction during rotation). Set retention to a sensible window (we use 90d). For keys, create a new key version to rotate; you can rewrap DEKs to the new key version URI.

liz: Audit logging: enable diagnostic settings for Microsoft.KeyVault to send to Log Analytics and Event Hub (for SIEM). Create alerts on Delete/Purge/SetRole/SetPolicy operations. If you need long-term immutable logs for compliance, route to a storage account with immutability policy.

infra-bot: diagnostic: created diagnostic setting "kv-audit-prod" -> LogAnalytics workspace (created by liz) at 09:12 UTC

anita: Plan I'm going to propose in the RFC: 1) avoid trying to use system-assigned MSIs across tenants; either (a) deploy a tiny per-tenant access proxy with a user-assigned identity, or (b) provision a service principal in the KV tenant for cross-tenant apps (with limited scope). 2) Use Azure RBAC data-plane roles for Key Vault. 3) Use KV (Managed HSM if required) as KEK for envelope encryption, store wrap metadata (key id + version), and implement a rewrap job (proactive or lazy). 4) Enable diagnostics -> LA/EventHub, soft-delete + purge-protect. 5) Add rotation runbooks and alerting for failed unwraps.

mike: Also check tenant tenant-level restrictions: conditional access, PIM, or guest invite restrictions can block SP/guest scenarios. If those are locked down, the per-tenant proxy approach is simpler operationally.

anita: Thanks all — I'll draft RFC and list options + cost/operational tradeoffs. If anyone has an internal doc or previous RFC we can copy, drop it here. :thumbsup:
